title: Edge handoff: adaptive kernel affinity selector with confidence curation and safe retraction
creator: Alicia Chen
description:
Problem: We need a low-latency path for tentative outputs that can safely be committed when fast kernels produce high-confidence tokens, and gracefully retracted when confidence or kernel affinity deteriorates. Current speculative routing favors model-level fallbacks but lacks a fine-grained kernel affinity signal and an operational playbook for safe retraction (retract = undo optimistic commit without user-visible corruption).

Proposal summary: Implement an 'edge handoff' subsystem in the runtime that does three things: (1) maintain a kernel-affinity oracle that recommends execution kernels based on attention profile, sequence-length distribution, and throughput envelope; (2) compute a streaming confidence curation score for prefill/tentative decode outputs (confidence derived from logits stability, acceptance heuristics, and small auxiliary checks); (3) expose a safe retraction protocol and fallback gating that can un-commit optimistic output if acceptance metrics fall below a configurable threshold.

Goals and non-goals: Goals: reduce P95 latency on fast-path by 10-25% for workloads with short responses while keeping regression in generation quality below 1% by our eval suite; provide deterministic rollback with no duplicated tokens in streamed responses. Non-goals: model training changes, wholesale kernel rewrites (we leverage existing kernels and scheduling primitives).

Design highlights: 
- Kernel-affinity oracle: lightweight estimator that ingests recent request histograms (seq lengths, attention pattern summary like average key density), hardware fingerprint (SM count, memory bandwidth), and model meta (quantization profile) to select a preferred kernel variant and an optimism score. Implemented as a pluggable policy with a simple exponential moving average state.
- Confidence curation: compute rolling acceptance score using: softmax temperature-normalized top-k stability across the first N candidate tokens; KV-cache hit ratio for prefix tokens; decode-time margin (top1 - top2) smoothed over token window. Map these signals to a single 0..1 acceptance metric and record a reason code vector for debugging.
- Safe retraction protocol: optimistic commit uses a short-lived local envelope. If acceptance metric falls < threshold T_retract within M tokens, runtime issues a retract event. The streaming API sends a retract marker and an alternative replacement fragment when possible; clients with older SDKs will receive minimal fallback (truncate + note). System ensures idempotency by including commit IDs in token frames.

Telemetry & metrics: acceptance_rate, retract_rate, false_retract_rate (measured by offline eval where ground-truth acceptability is known), fastpath_success_latency (P50/P95), kernel_misselect_rate (cases where fallback kernel produced acceptance > preferred), and per-reason-code counters. Dashboards and alerts configured in Console.

Rollout plan: 
- Alpha: internal-only, flag-controlled, small fleet in us-west with synthetic load and canary prompts (2 weeks).
- Beta: opt-in for select customers, additional monitoring retention and customer impact checks (4 weeks).
- GA: enable by default with conservative thresholds and automated rollback triggers (6+ weeks).

Testing & validation: unit tests for oracle heuristics, end-to-end synthetic harness with randomized attention profiles, offline eval against our prompt corpus for quality regressions, chaos tests simulating kernel OOM and slow kernels to validate retract pathways.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/RI/Edge+Handoff+Kernel+Affinity, implementation PR will live at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231, and a dashboard prototype at https://grafana.redwood.example/d/edge-handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Edge handoff selects a preferred kernel for >90% of fast-path requests within 1ms overhead
Acceptance metric computed and emitted per-request in trace logs
Retract event reverses optimistic commit without duplicated tokens in streaming integration tests
No >1% quality regression on eval corpus for earliest 2 rollout weeks
Telemetry surfaces kernel_misselect_rate and retract_rate in Console
